# Text Features {#sec-text-features}

```{r}
#| label: setup-text
source("_common.R")
```


## Conditional text

There are several ways to include text optionally.
First, we can use in-line helpers such as `dlm_is_pdf()` or `dlm_is_html()`, which can be used to determine the type of output.
For example, this is the `r ifelse(dlm_is_pdf(), "PDF", "website")` version of this report.

We can also include or exclude entire paragraphs using the the `.content-visible` class with a div.

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
Read this report chapter by chapter in the browser, or download the complete PDF from the button above.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="typst"}
The report is also available as a searchable website at <https://dynamiclearningmaps.org>.
:::


## Callouts {#sec-callouts}

Callouts can be used to draw attention to some text.
Create a callout with:

````
::: {.callout-note}
## Callout title

Here is the callout text.
:::
````

::: {.callout-note}
## Note callout

Create a note callout using the `.callout-note` class.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Tip callout

Create a tip callout using the `.callout-tip` class.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## Important callout

Create an important callout using the `.callout-important` class.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Warning callout

Create a warning callout using the `.callout-warning` class.
:::

::: {.callout-caution}
## Caution callout

Create a caution callout using the `.callout-caution` class.
:::

## Code

Inline code renders as you would expect (e.g., `function_name()`).
We can also include code chunks.

```{r}
#| label: test-code
#| echo: true

library(tidyverse)

penguins |>
  as_tibble() |>
  filter(species == "Adelie")
```

## Cross references

We can cross reference sections.
For example, callouts are described in @sec-callouts.
Or we can reference subheadings such as @sec-heading-3.
Or we can reference another chapter.
Figures are described in @sec-figures.

We can also reference tables and figures like @tbl-example1 and @fig-example1.


```{r}
#| label: tbl-example1
#| tbl-cap: An example table caption.

set.seed(2015)
tibble(
  state = sample(state.name, size = 5),
  n = sample(1000:100000, size = 5)
) |>
  gt() |>
  gt_atlas()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-example1
#| fig-cap: An example figure caption
#| fig-alt: A scatterplot of penguins.

ggplot(penguins, aes(x = flipper_len, y = bill_len)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = species, shape = species))
```


## Citations

We can include a normal reference [@measr].
Or we can include in text, such as with @clark2016.
We can also include an abbreviation, like for the loglinear cognitive diagnostic model [LCDM\; @henson2009].

## Equations

Equations can also be rendered, numbered, and references as shown in @eq-dcm.

$$
P(X_j = x_j) = \sum_{c=1}^C\nu_c \prod_{i=1}^I\pi_{ic}^{x_{ij}}(1-\pi_{ic})^{1 - x_{ij}}
$$ {#eq-dcm}

We can also render math inline.
For example, the intercept of @eq-lcdm, $\lambda_{i,0}$, determines the probability of a correct response for a nonmaster, and the main effect $\lambda_{i,1}$ is the increase in log-odds associated with mastery.

$$
\pi_{ic} = P(X_{ic} = 1|\alpha_c) = \frac{\exp(\lambda_{i,0} + \lambda_{i,1}\alpha_c)}{1 + \exp(\lambda_{i,0} + \lambda_{i,1}\alpha_c)}
$$ {#eq-lcdm}
